references.text: Aaron and his sons were commanded not to leave the entrance of the tabernacle, reflecting the same command to remain at the entrance of the tent of meeting.
Earlier in the same chapter, the priests are commanded not to leave the entrance of the tent of meeting for seven days during the consecration period.
The expression 'keep watch for the Lord' (שָׁמַר מִשְׁמֶרֶת יְהוָה) is used similarly to mean keeping the Lord's command.
The Levites were to keep watch at the tent of meeting and take care of everything belonging to the tabernacle, using the same terminology as in Leviticus 8:35.
The seven-day consecration of the priests parallels the consecration ritual described in Exodus.
The warning 'so that you may not die' is repeated as a consequence for failing to keep the Lord's statutes.
The same expression about keeping watch over the sanctuary to prevent wrath from falling upon the people of Israel.
Ezekiel describes the Levites keeping watch at the temple, using the same terminology of 'keeping watch' (שָׁמַר מִשְׁמֶרֶת).
